title: Trace Ops Cookbook — Weekly Lab Notes (2028-05-09)
body:
Purpose:
Quick lab-style notes from this week’s Trace Ops sync. Focused on three concurrent pilots: dashboard pruning heuristics, adaptive sampling prototype (edge buckets), and a small-cost audit on span ingestion. Informal — captures open questions, live-run numbers, and next-step experiments.

Attendees:
- Aisha (lead note-taker)
- Marco (dashboard author)
- Priya (cost telemetry)
- Evan (sampling infra)
- Zara (SRE oncall)
- Short cameo from Product (Ravi) for rollout constraints

Standup snippets (5–10m each):
- Aisha: rolled the lightweight dashboard-prune job to canary (svc-telemetry-canary). Observed 12% reduction in dashboard query latency for the expensive 90th pct slice; more below.
- Marco: iterated on the prune rule UI — added a "last-accessed" column and a dry-run toggle.
- Priya: flagged two customers with unexpected span volume spikes on 2028-05-07 (runtime traces from dedupe job). Billing alert muted but cost delta looks real.
- Evan: sampling prototype deployed to 10% of requests for edge-region; early signal shows sample retention of tail errors is preserved with stratified sampling.
- Zara: SLO noise increased in eu-west-2 on 2028-05-08 during the prune canary; probable correlation with the prune job hitting a legacy dashboard with an unpaginated elastic query.

Deep dive 1 — Dashboard pruning experiment (canary):
- Hypothesis: Removing/archiving rarely-used heavy dashboards will lower downstream trace query latency and reduce span ingestion spikes triggered by dashboard refreshes.
- Approach: sample set = 72 dashboards tagged "heavy" (cost > 1.5 CPU-min/day) and not viewed in 90 days. Canary target = internal analytics team.
- Result (canary window 2028-05-06 — 2028-05-09):
  - Median query latency (canary hosts): -3% (negligible)
  - P95 latency (dashboard queries touching traces): -12%
  - Span ingestion rate (cluster-telemetry-1): -8% during scheduled refresh hours (0200–0500 UTC)
  - Cost impact (estimated): ~0.9% monthly L0 savings if scaled org-wide (~$7.2k/mo).
- Incident: One dashboard had a long-running scroll-based query against a 1B-span index; prune job disabled for that dashboard until query is re-written.
- Decision: proceed with phased rollout but add an automatic "query-explanation" capture prior to archiving to present to owners. Action: Marco to add capture by EOD 2028-05-10.

Deep dive 2 — Adaptive sampling pilot (edge buckets):
- Goal: keep error/latency-signal fidelity while reducing span ingestion from noisy mobile clients.
- Implementation notes:
  - Stratified sampling by (region, client-version, error-class).
  - Default rate = 1% for non-error low-cardinality buckets; boosted to 100% for error buckets and 10% for suspect versions.
  - Deployed to 10% of traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
- Early metrics (72h):
  - Overall spans ingested from pilot cohort: -64%
  - Error-span retention: 98.4% (target >= 97%)
  - Latency-correlated spans preserved at ~95% for p99 error traces
- Notes: we saw one false-negative pattern where an off-by-one deserialization error produced non-error traces but was root cause for downstream incidents. Evan: add rule to route deserialization fingerprints to 100% sampling even if not flagged as error.
- Decision: expand to 25% after adding the fingerprint rule and a short backfill window to capture missed cases.

Cost telemetry audit (micro findings):
- Priya ran a delta analysis across May's first week vs baseline April W4: overall telemetry tokenized bill +4.1% but span-portion only +1.2% (surprising given April infra churn).
- Two outliers identified:
  1) dedupe-job-v2 (customer-facing batch) that began spewing debug traces after toggling V2 metrics. Estimated incremental cost: $2.8k/mo. Owner: data-platform team (linked JIRA: DP-889).
  2) internal-loadtest harness left at debug = true for 36 hours; extra spans ~3.2M; mitigating run cost ~ $320. Owner: perf-engineering; mitigation checklist items below.

Correlations and trending:
- Span size distribution shifted slightly (median size +4 bytes) due to added metadata in gRPC headers — low impact but worth condensing header keys.
- The sample retention changes from the pilot coupled with dashboard pruning explain the observed -8% ingestion in the canary cluster.

Runbook edit notes (temporary):
- Add step: before pruning, run query-explain and capture slow scrolls.
- Add step: if prune touches dashboards with cross-org ownership, open "prune-review" label in JIRA and notify owners 72h prior.
- Add step: sampling pilot must include a 48h backfill window where we keep raw spans in a limited-size cold store for forensic backfills.

Action items (owner, deadline):
- Marco: implement query-explain capture & dry-run UI flag; due 2028-05-10.
- Evan: add deserialization fingerprint rule and expand sampling to 25% post-qa; due 2028-05-12.
- Priya: publish a short cost digest for May week-1 with clear owners for the two outlier sources; due 2028-05-11.
- Zara: add automated guard in prune job to skip unpaginated queries and emit alert; due 2028-05-13.
- Aisha: draft stakeholder email template for dashboard archival notices; due 2028-05-11.

Open questions / parking lot:
- How long do we keep the cold-store backfill before permanent deletion? (cost tradeoff) — Priya to model 7/14/30 day cost curves.
- Should the default heavy-dashboard threshold be dynamic (based on recent cost per owner) instead of static CPU-min/day? Marco to prototype dynamic scoring.
- Can we integrate sampling fingerprints with the incident timeline tool to auto-attach probable root-span? Longer-term idea.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Remember: customers hate surprise deletions — keep the UI messages explicit: "Archive: reduces trace query latency; you can restore within 14 days."
- Check with Legal before automating deletion windows for regulated customers.

Quick links / references used in meeting:
- Confluence: trace-cookbook (see "Prune heuristics")
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-4217 (sampling prototype), DP-889 (dedupe job), PERF-1222 (loadtest debug left-on)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/trace-tooling/pull/233 (sampling stratifier improvements)

Next sync (tentative): 2028-05-16 09:30 PT — focus list: rollout plan for pruning (phase 2), sampling expansion checklist, backfill cold-store sizing.

End notes:
- Tone: lab notes, not a final runbook. Please add comments inline in Confluence if you want items elevated.
- If you are listed as owner above and need bandwidth re-assignment, ping Aisha (aisha@redwood.com) or drop in #obs-ops.
